headline_draft: OpenAI retires Custom GPTs, migrates users to plugins as GPT Store strategy shifts
summary: OpenAI quietly closed Custom GPT creation and publishing on September 19, 2026, restricting creation and public deployment to business accounts only. With 3 million GPTs in total but only 159,000 public and active, the policy fundamentally reframes the three-way platform choice: OpenAI's plugin model versus Anthropic's Claude Skills versus Google's Gemini Gems. The move signals OpenAI's shift away from user-generated content toward managed, vetted plugins with reusable instructions and connected apps. This leaves teams that relied on Custom GPTs to either migrate to plugins or switch platforms.
why_pm: As a PM evaluating AI agent customization platforms, you need to understand which ecosystem you're actually betting on. This retirement fundamentally changes the playbook for building personalized agents on ChatGPT and raises the question: is plugin adoption the future, or should teams prototype on Claude Skills or Gemini instead?
key_facts: OpenAI closed Custom GPT creation as of August 16, 2026 for most users
3 million GPTs exist total; only 159,000 are public and active
Migration path to plugins (reusable instructions + connected apps) now primary offering
Restricts creation to business accounts and workspace admins

headline_draft: GPT-6 Astra launches at $2.50/$50 per million tokens on Claude Skills platform choice becomes existential
summary: OpenAI's flagship GPT-6 Astra model launched September 3, 2026 at $2.50 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens on the standard API tier (per CloudZero). This is the new frontier model baseline. Meanwhile, the agent framework landscape has crystallized into three distinct platforms: OpenAI (API-first, GPT-centric), Anthropic (Skills + Computer Use + Files), and Google (Gemini with custom workflows). The pricing and feature set of each now determines not just how fast you can prototype, but which agent behaviors you can afford to run at scale—multi-agent loops on Astra add up fast.
why_pm: Token economics now directly impact your agent design. Multi-agent workflows with high reasoning steps can exceed your cost budget quickly on frontier models. You need to understand your platform's pricing structure, token usage per trace, and fallback models (smaller, cheaper, less capable) before committing to an agent architecture. A well-designed agent that routes expensive thinking work to cheaper models can cut costs 40–60%.
key_facts: GPT-6 Astra: $2.50 per million input tokens, $50 per million output tokens
Multi-agent workflows accumulate token costs quickly across model calls
Teams should instrument token usage per trace early to avoid surprises at scale
Route inference to cheaper models where possible (similar to Sakana Fugu Max 40–60% savings in earlier digest)
